title: Copyright and fair use
examples: If I find a song online, do I need permission to use it in my school play?
What is the difference between copyright and public domain?
Can I use someone's photo for my science project without asking them?

explain.say: When someone creates something new, they often own the rights to it.
Copyright law gives the creator exclusive rights over their original work.

items: Original works are protected by law.
The creator usually holds the initial rights.

explain.say: A licence is permission that allows you to use copyrighted material legally.

draw.text: Licences grant permission to use work.

explain.say: Creative Commons licences are easy ways to share work with clear rules.
For example, a photo might have a Creative Commons licence for reuse.

items: Row 2: CC BY | Attribution | Must credit creator
Row 3: CC BY-ND | No Derivatives | Cannot change the work

explain.say: In everyday life, you see copyright when using music in a video.

draw.text: Real life: Music in a video

faq.q: Can I use any picture I find online?
faq.a: No, you cannot use any picture you find online without checking the copyright status first. Most images are protected by copyright law. You should look for images marked as public domain or under a specific licence.
asks: Do I need permission for online pictures?
Is everything online free to use?

faq.q: What is the difference between copyright and public domain?
faq.a: Copyright gives the creator exclusive rights, meaning they control use. Public domain means the work is free for anyone to use without restriction or permission.
asks: What does 'public domain' mean for art?

faq.a: Fair use is a legal concept that allows limited use of copyrighted material without permission for purposes like criticism or education. However, the rules for fair use can be complex.
asks: Does fair use mean I can use anything I want?

faq.q: What is the easiest way to share my work legally?
faq.a: Using Creative Commons licences is often the easiest way. These licences let you choose exactly how others can use your work while still giving you some control.
asks: How do I make my work shareable?
What is the best way to share art online?

faq.q: Do I need to credit the original creator?
faq.a: Yes, most licences, especially Creative Commons ones, require you to give credit to the original creator. This is called attribution and is very important.

facts: Copyright protects the original expression of an idea, not the idea itself.
Creative Commons licences provide standardized ways to share rights.
Attribution, or giving credit, is required by many licences.
Public domain works have no copyright restrictions.

quiz.say: A photographer wants to use a picture in a magazine without changing it. Which licence type is best if they only need to give credit?
quiz.why: This licence allows others to use the work, provided they simply give credit to the original creator.

wrong.1: This means no one can use it without direct permission.
wrong.2: This prevents using the work for any money-making purpose.
wrong.3: This means no rights are held at all, which might not be what the photographer intends.

quiz.say: A student wants to use a famous painting for a school presentation and needs to change some colours. What must they check for?

options.show: If they cite the artist's name
options.say: If they cite the artist's name

options.show: If the school pays for it
options.say: If the school pays for it

quiz.why: The student must check if the licence allows 'derivatives,' which means changing or adapting the original work.

wrong.0: Citing the name is good, but it does not grant permission to modify the work.
wrong.2: Age alone does not guarantee it is in the public domain.
wrong.3: Payment does not automatically grant usage rights.

quiz.say: If a work is in the public domain, what does that mean for its use?

options.show: It is free for anyone to use without needing permission.
options.say: It is free for anyone to use without needing permission.

options.show: It can only be used for education
options.say: It can only be used for education

quiz.why: Public domain means the work's rights have expired or were never established, making it freely available for all.

wrong.0: The definition of public domain means no specific licence is needed.
wrong.2: While old works are often in the public domain, it is not the only way.
wrong.3: Public domain works can generally be used for any purpose.
